e-15602.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15602.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/a664a3af1ba466491d209dadd32a3be026a5179ac2d0281b55f30917f9ab016b.png)
What would be the vector equation of the line?
e-15602.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+2t \\ 5t \\ 1-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 5t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

e-15603.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15603.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/f161e07945eb3fe2350a56ab5cb96fa0ae2d055eb3b4cc633abfae30839ec76f.png)
Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
e-15603.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-t \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,3,1)$ and is parallel to the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/11701a2d63851a3f241d8bd905693abaaa6eda6fe4ba0c5710c92d8189595ffd.png)

before.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=−3y=5tz=−2 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[−20−3]+t[050],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[30−2]+t[150],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[302]+t[050],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−30−2]+t[050],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−302]+t[0−5−5],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Separating the constant coordinates from the coefficients of t gives r=(-3,0,-2)+t(0,5,0), which reproduces x=-3, y=5t, and z=-2. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3 \\ y=5t \\ z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5t \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3 \\ y=5t \\ z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5t \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 2
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=5y=4tz=7 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[040]+t[507],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=t[040],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=t[507],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
None of the listed
e
r=[507]+t[040],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant coordinates give the position vector (5,0,7), and the coefficients of t give the direction vector (0,4,0). Option e therefore reproduces x=5, y=4t, and z=7.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=4t \\ z=7\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4t \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=4t \\ z=7\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4t \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=1+ty=2−tz=0 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[120]+t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[1−10]+t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
None of the listed
Submit

decision.explanation: Separating constants and coefficients of t gives r=(1,2,0)+t(1,-1,0). Its coordinates are (1+t,2-t,0), exactly the given equations, so option b is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+t \\ 2-t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+t \\ 2-t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 4
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=13−8ty=7tz=−7−3t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[−1307]+t[−8−73],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[130−7]+t[−37−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[130−7]+t[−87−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[130−7]+t[−8−73],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[1307]+t[873],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant terms form (13,0,-7), and the coefficients of t form (-8,7,-3). Thus option c gives coordinates (13-8t,7t,-7-3t), matching all three equations.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=13-8t \\ y=7t \\ z=-7-3t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13-8t \\ 7t \\ -7-3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8t \\ 7t \\ -3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 4
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=13−8ty=7tz=−7−3t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[−1307]+t[−8−73],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[130−7]+t[−37−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[130−7]+t[−87−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[130−7]+t[−8−73],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[1307]+t[873],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

These parametric equations are equivalent to [xyz]=[13−8t7t−7−3t][xyz]=[130−7]+[−8t7t−3t][xyz]=[130−7]+t[−87−3]r=[130−7]+t[−87−3], where t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option c. Its coordinates are (13-8t,7t,-7-3t), exactly the given equations. Submitted option b swaps the x and z direction coefficients and describes a different line.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=13-8t \\ y=7t \\ z=-7-3t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13-8t \\ 7t \\ -7-3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8t \\ 7t \\ -3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

$$

Question 5
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=5y=2+3tz=−t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[520]+t[03−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=t[520],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[03−1]+t[520],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=t[03−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
None of the listed
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant terms give (5,2,0), and the coefficients of t give (0,3,-1). Option a therefore has coordinates (5,2+3t,-t), matching the given equations.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=2+3t \\ z=-t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2+3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

EXPLANATION

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=2+3t \\ z=-t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2+3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

before.name: Question 6
before.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t-1 \\ y=-t+1 \\ z=-t-1\end{aligned}

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=t−1y=−t+1z=−t−1 Find a vector that is parallel to the line.

decision.explanation: The coefficients of t in x, y, and z are 1, -1, and -1, so (1,-1,-1) is a direction vector parallel to the line. This is option e.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t-1 \\ y=-t+1 \\ z=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}t-1 \\ -t+1 \\ -t-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-1,1,-1)$   and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t-1 \\ y=-t+1 \\ z=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}t-1 \\ -t+1 \\ -t-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-1,1,-1)$   and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
